newsitem.title: USA: Teamsters, Union resume talks in Washington.
newsitem.headline: Teamsters, Union resume talks in Washington.

text.p: Talks between Teamsters union and United Parcel Service officials resumed in Washington on Friday as the strike at the world's largest package carrier dragged into its fifth day.
The parties were to pick up where they left off after 10-1/2 hours of talks that started Thursday afternoon but produced little progress.

"No significant progress was made," UPS negotiator Dave Murray said of Thursday night's talks as he arrived for Friday's meeting. He emphasised that UPS was sticking to its bargaining position. "We feel it's a great offer."
Teamsters President Ron Carey simply said "No" when asked if there had been progress on specific issues. "The company seems to be stuck on its proposal," he said.

Nevertheless, the two sides will keep talking with the help of federal mediator John Calhoun Wells. Labour Secretary Alexis Herman said she had talked to Carey and UPS Chairman Jim Kelly on Friday, urging them to redouble efforts to settle the strike.

The walkout has choked off the delivery of nearly 12 million packages a day across the United States, hitting the mail order catalogue business especially hard, as well as deliveries of some medical supplies.
